note: Re-judged 2026-10-21 (independent auditor, authored none of the change). RFC 8277 Section 3.2.2: "It can decide not to propagate the route to the given peer.  In that case, if a previous route with the same AFI, SAFI, and prefix (but with fewer labels) has already been propagated to that peer, that route MUST be withdrawn from that peer using the procedure of Section 2.4." mpReachNextHopHandler moved in 7b0bf3a723 and f70588873f, and both hunks are confined to the noNextHop arms (noNextHop = !fam.NeedsNextHop(), FlowSpec only): a 4- or 16-octet Set is now kept for a FlowSpec redirect-to-IP target, any other width is written as the empty field, and the comment above it changed to match. The arms a next-hop family takes (the width table 4/12/16/24/32/48 and familyAdmitsNextHopOctets) are byte-identical, so a VPN-IPv6 or labeled-unicast rewrite behaves as at the last judgement. mpReachNextHopHandler still replaces the next hop and retains the whole NLRI with no recipient label-count decision; BuildLabeledUnicastNLRIBytes still serializes every supplied label; internal/core/bgp/capability carries no Multiple Labels Capability, so no per-peer label limit exists to decline propagation against and no fewer-label withdrawal is produced. No test is tagged. The {gap} annotation remains accurate; the gap stands and does not authorize implementation.
